proof_summary: The continued fraction is evaluated as a rational expression with numerator proportional to \(T(n)=(n+1)^2-5\); if \(T(n)=pm\), size, factorial-divisibility, and parity arguments show that reduction cancels exactly the factor \(2m\) but not \(p\), leaving numerator \(p\). Quadratic reciprocity makes \(5\) a square modulo every such \(p\), so choosing \(n=x-1\) from \(x^2\equiv5\pmod p\) gives \(p\mid T(n)\), with the small exceptional case handled directly.
